events.title: Antioch surrenders to the Arab armies
events.description: After the Battle of the Iron Bridge, Antioch surrendered to Muslim forces under Abu Ubayda. The fall of the great Syrian city was part of the rapid conquests that stripped Byzantium of its eastern provinces.
events.html: After the Battle of the Iron Bridge, Antioch surrendered to Muslim forces under Abu Ubayda. The fall of the great Syrian city was part of the rapid conquests that stripped Byzantium of its eastern provinces.

events.title: Arab and Persian pirates sack Guangzhou
events.description: During the An Lushan Rebellion in China, Arab and Persian pirates sacked the port of Guangzhou. In 760, in revenge, Chinese rebels killed thousands of Arabs and Persians in the Yangzhou massacre.
events.html: During the An Lushan Rebellion in China, Arab and Persian pirates sacked the port of Guangzhou. In 760, in revenge, Chinese rebels killed thousands of Arabs and Persians in the Yangzhou massacre.

events.title: Ranulf of Alife defeats Roger II of Sicily at Rignano
events.description: Near Rignano Garganico in Apulia, the rebel Ranulf of Alife, supported by troops left behind by Emperor Lothair III, defeated King Roger II of Sicily. Roger's ally Duke Sergius VII of Naples was killed, and Naples passed under Roger's direct rule.
events.html: Near Rignano Garganico in Apulia, the rebel Ranulf of Alife, supported by troops left behind by Emperor Lothair III, defeated King Roger II of Sicily. Roger's ally Duke Sergius VII of Naples was killed, and Naples passed under Roger's direct rule.

events.title: The Treaty of Tunis ends the Eighth Crusade
events.description: After Louis IX died of disease outside Tunis, his brother Charles of Anjou negotiated a treaty with the sultan of Tunis and the crusaders withdrew. Louis was canonised in 1297.
events.html: After Louis IX died of disease outside Tunis, his brother Charles of Anjou negotiated a treaty with the sultan of Tunis and the crusaders withdrew. Louis was canonised in 1297.

events.title: Castile and Portugal defeat the Marinids at Río Salado
events.description: Near Tarifa, the kings Alfonso XI of Castile and Afonso IV of Portugal defeated the Marinid sultan Abu al-Hasan and Yusuf I of Granada, who were besieging the town. It was the last major North African attempt to invade Iberia.

events.title: Henry VII is crowned, beginning the Tudor dynasty
events.description: Henry Tudor was crowned at Westminster Abbey two months after defeating Richard III at Bosworth. His marriage to Elizabeth of York united the rival houses of the Wars of the Roses.
events.html: Henry Tudor was crowned at Westminster Abbey two months after defeating Richard III at Bosworth. His marriage to Elizabeth of York united the rival houses of the Wars of the Roses.

events.title: The Armistice of Mudros takes the Ottomans out of the war
events.description: Ottoman and British representatives signed an armistice aboard HMS Agamemnon off Lemnos. Allied occupation and partition plans followed, provoking the Turkish national movement led by Mustafa Kemal.
events.html: Ottoman and British representatives signed an armistice aboard HMS Agamemnon off Lemnos. Allied occupation and partition plans followed, provoking the Turkish national movement led by Mustafa Kemal.

events.title: Orson Welles broadcasts The War of the Worlds
events.description: CBS aired Orson Welles's radio adaptation of H. G. Wells's novel as a series of mock news bulletins about a Martian landing in New Jersey. Some listeners were alarmed, though newspapers exaggerated the 'panic'.
events.html: CBS aired Orson Welles's radio adaptation of H. G. Wells's novel as a series of mock news bulletins about a Martian landing in New Jersey. Some listeners were alarmed, though newspapers exaggerated the 'panic'.

events.title: The Soviet Union tests the Tsar Bomba
events.description: A Soviet bomber dropped the largest nuclear weapon ever exploded over Novaya Zemlya in the Arctic. Its yield of about 50 megatons was some 3,000 times that of the Hiroshima bomb.
